description: Team BackSpace is a 100% all-female multidisciplinary team from Ceará, Brazil, driven by a passion for science and technology. Composed of 5 students from IFCE and UFC (two developers and three designers), we are proud members of the Apple Developer Academy. By blending robust technical skills with user-centered design and accessibility, we strive to create immersive, meaningful digital experiences that educate and inspire our users.
summary:
The project consists of a web-based game developed for children, adolescents, and aerospace engineering enthusiasts, which narrates the story of an extraterrestrial being interested in learning more about humanity. While exploring the universe in pursuit of new discoveries, our protagonist encounters discarded NASA materials and brings them back to life, recounting their historical trajectory and their impact on aerospace technological development. Through this initiative, we aim to impart knowledge to the youth and enthusiasts regarding projects that, despite being currently inactive, have had a profound impact on the history of space exploration and ought not to be forgotten.

The application was developed in GDScript, utilizing the Godot engine to construct the game's mechanics and flow. It features a completely original and unique design, which evokes a sense of belonging and connection with the extraterrestrial's narrative and the elements she discovers. Thus, we seek to bring people closer to this abandoned, yet never forgotten, hardware, transcending spatio-temporal limitations.
details:
Backspace

Backspace is a 2D narrative and educational space-exploration game where players follow Lyra, a curious space traveler journeying across our Solar System to discover 7 real, historical NASA spacecraft and rovers that have gone silent after completing their missions.

BackSpace Main Menu.

How Does Our Solution Work

The game transforms real NASA data into an interactive, story-driven experience. The radar dynamically calculates the nearest unvisited missions from the ship's current coordinates, allowing players to warp across the Solar System until all 7 explorers are remembered.

  • Discovery & The Pioneer Plaque: The story begins when Lyra stumbles upon Pioneer 10 drifting in deep space. By scanning it and recovering a copy of its famous Pioneer Plaque, she unlocks her ship's Solar Radar.
  • First-Person Spacecraft Encounters: At each destination, players view the spacecraft floating outside the cockpit window and activate the Window Scanner. During the scan, the spacecraft itself speaks in the first person, sharing when it launched, what it discovered, the hardships it faced, and when its last signal reached Earth.

Scanning a forgotten explorer in first-person view.

  • Interactive Mission Report Diary: Every encounter unlocks a tabbed page in Lyra's physical binder. This blends official NASA technical specifications (TYPE, LAUNCH, TARGET, OBJECTIVE) and verifiable source links with Lyra's personal handwritten notes.

The Mission Report Diary blending NASA data with Lyra's notes.

Design Process & Design Thinking

A core strength of Backspace is its distinct visual identity and user-centered design. We adopted a Design Thinking approach, heavily relying on Figma for wireframing, mood-boarding, and interactive prototyping to test our UI flows and accessibility features before writing any code.

  • Iterative Prototyping in Figma: We mapped out the entire user journey—from the radar navigation logic to the dialogue layouts—ensuring a seamless and intuitive User Experience (UX).
  • Diegetic Interface Design: To heighten immersion, the UI is designed to exist within the game world. The scanner data projects directly onto the ship's glass window, and the mission logs are collected in a tactile, physical paper binder.
  • Typography & Color Palette: We intentionally contrasted cold, technical monospace fonts (IBM Plex Mono) representing NASA's data with warm, human handwriting fonts for Lyra's notes. The deep-space color palette maintains high contrast to ensure readability and compliance with accessibility standards.

Early wireframes and interactive UI prototypes developed in Figma.

Benefits and Impact

Our intended impact is to humanize space science and preserve the legacy of robotic exploration. We want to inspire students and the general public to see these silent machines not as space debris, but as time capsules of human curiosity.

Key Benefits:

  • Empathy-Driven STEM Learning: By turning dry technical telemetry into first-person memoirs told by the probes themselves, players emotionally connect with space history and retain scientific facts effortlessly.
  • Built-in Accessibility: Features a dynamic Large Text mode (scaling the entire UI theme, fonts, and margins by 1.6x), a Reduce Motion mode (disabling warp shaders for vestibular sensitivity), adjustable dialogue speed, and automatic checkpoint saving.
  • Zero-Install Web Access: Built to run directly in any modern web browser via WebAssembly/HTML5, making it immediately accessible in classrooms, museums, and low-end devices.

Built-in accessibility features ensure everyone can explore the cosmos.

Creativity and Innovation

  • Reversed Perspective: Instead of telling NASA's history from a human control room on Earth, the player experiences our Solar System through the eyes of an outsider piecing together humanity's story from the machines we left behind.
  • The Pioneer Plaque as a Core Mechanic: In real life, the Plaque was a message for whoever might find it. In our game, Lyra actually finds it—realizing "A message for whoever found it… I think that means me"—and uses its map to unlock her radar.
  • Code-Free Content Expansion: Designed with a modular data-driven architecture and a custom editor verification tool. Educators can add new spacecraft and translations using simple .json and .tres files without touching code.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Game Engine: Godot Engine 4.7 (GL Compatibility rendering pipeline for broad Web and Desktop support).
  • Coding Languages: GDScript (gameplay state machine, dynamic UI, proximity navigation) and GDShader (procedural starfield and warp-speed visual effects).
  • Data Structures: JSON and Godot Custom Resources (.tres) for localized dialogue and mission databases.
  • Design Assets: Custom SVG vector graphics, PNG illustrations, dual-typography styling (IBM Plex Mono + handwriting fonts), and OGG Vorbis audio.
  • Design & Prototyping: Figma (UI/UX wireframing and mood boards).
  • Deployment: Exported to HTML5 / WebAssembly, hosted via Netlify, with version control via Git.
